subject: MAP: Performance validation & GPU fleet recommendation — Acme Payments
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@acme.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM EST
Subject: Performance validation + MAP for upcoming POC

Diego —

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We’re ready to sanity-check our performance assumptions before we commit to a Dedicated capacity plan. Two asks from our side:

1) A short MAP that lays out the evaluation plan + timeline so we can align procurement and our infra team.
2) A small benchmarking run comparing A100 vs H100 vs L40S (and a sample MIG profile) for the models we plan to serve (13B & 70B family). Key metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency per-GPU.

We expect production traffic to be bursty (peaks ~120 concurrent requests, baseline ~8 QPS) and we plan to serve a mix of streaming and non-streaming responses. Security and data residency are in scope but we can handle those through the Private offering later — right now we need numbers to size the committed capacity.

Can you put together a one-page MAP + a short perf plan and share next steps? We’re targeting an internal decision by early Dec.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Payments

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a first-pass MAP (acme_map_v0.1.xlsx) that includes: scope, evaluation matrix, proposed test harness, and a draft timeline. Highlights:

- Models: 13B decoder-only (quantized int8/4 variants) and 70B baseline (fp16 + quantized).
- HW candidates: A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S 48GB (and representative MIG slices: 7g / 4g).
- Metrics: TTFT (streaming and non-streaming), p50/p95/p99, sustained tokens/sec, tokens/second per GPU at target concurrency, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
- Test types: synthetic replay (to stress throughput), live-replay (sample of your dev traffic), and cold-start series to measure KV/cache warmup.
- Proposed run window: pilot tests next week (Nov 16–18), full suite the week of Nov 22.

Internal note for Karthik/Marissa/Sergio: can you review the attached MAP and add specific perf test definitions (scripts, batch sizes, request mixes) and recommended MIG configurations? I’ll share the consolidated MAP with Acme once we have pilot numbers.

Attachments: acme_map_v0.1.xlsx (MAP draft)

Thanks —

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 09:20 AM PST
Subject: Re: Performance validation + MAP for upcoming POC

Diego / team —

Quick comments on the MAP and proposed perf harness:

1) Test methodology (recommendation)
   - Use two modes: (A) replay of representative requests (real prompt set from Acme, sanitized) with token-by-token streaming enabled; (B) synthetic throughput stress (short prompts, high batch sizes) to measure max tokens/sec.
   - For TTFT, capture client-observed time to first token (include network + server dispatch). We’ll run both streaming (first-token measured when server sends 1st stream chunk) and non-streaming (time until first token in final response).

2) HW profiles and MIG
   - Full GPU: measure A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB.
   - MIG: include 7g (best for large 13B), 4g (economy), and a denser 1g slice to test density tradeoffs. Be explicit about MIG partitioning overhead (~10–20% expected).

3) SLO targets (initial suggestions)
   - TTFT (streaming): p95 < 300ms for 13B small responses; p95 < 700ms for 70B (depends on prompt length).
   - Sustained tokens/sec: target 10–20k tokens/sec per H100 for 13B workload (single-streamed requests), adjust after pilot.

4) Bench scripts and artifacts
   - I pushed perf-specs-hwmatrix.csv with batch/buffer profiles and concurrency sweeps. We should capture per-step GPU utilization, NVLink throughput, and memory swap counts.

Caveat: MIG gives density but increases head-of-line latency variance. For Acme’s bursty traffic we should prioritize a mix: H100 for latency-critical endpoints, MIG-backed pools for high-density background endpoints.

Attaching: perf-specs-hwmatrix.csv

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infra Performance, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 2:45 PM PST
Subject: Re: Performance validation + MAP for upcoming POC — pilot results

Diego / team / Elena (cc’d on final) —

We completed the pilot runs (small curated set from Acme, plus synthetic sweeps). High-level findings below; full CSVs attached.

Executive summary:
- H100 (80GB) vs A100 (80GB): H100 delivered ~22–28% higher sustained throughput on 13B decoder workloads with our current runtime (FlashAttention + fused kernels). TTFT for streaming requests improved modestly (~10–15% p95).
- L40S (48GB): good cost point for mixed batches; on 70B runs we observed more frequent ephemeral memory copies which increased TTFT p99 by ~12–18% compared to H100.
- MIG vs Full GPU: a 7g MIG slice achieved ~78–88% of a full GPU’s throughput on 13B (throughput penalty ~12–22% depending on batch mix). MIG gives better density (3–4x effective concurrent user slots) but increases p99 variance.

Selected numbers (13B / streaming / median across runs):
- H100: 14.8k tokens/sec, p95 TTFT 260ms, p99 370ms, effective concurrency per GPU at target SLO ~48
- A100: 11.9k tokens/sec, p95 TTFT 300ms, p99 440ms, effective concurrency per GPU at target SLO ~36
- L40S: 10.2k tokens/sec, p95 TTFT 320ms, p99 470ms, effective concurrency ~30
- 7g MIG (on A100): ~9.6k tokens/sec, p95 TTFT 340ms

Notes / interpretation:
- H100 shines for 13B streaming—lower tokens/sec cost for latency SLOs. For 70B, the difference narrows (memory bandwidth and ft kernels limit uplift).
- MIG is compelling for high-density read-only workloads; for Acme’s bursty, low-latency checkout flows we recommend a hybrid strategy.

Attachments: benchmark-results-h100.csv, a100-h100-l40s-summary.pdf

Recommendation (short):
- Phase 1 (pilot): Use H100-backed pool for the latency-sensitive checkout endpoints (13B family).
- Phase 2 (scale/cost): Mix in A100 MIG pools for background/batch endpoints and fallbacks.

Happy to walk through numbers with Acme next week.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP + benchmark deliverables and next steps (timeline + approvals)

Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear ask — quick summary and next steps below. Please see the attached consolidated MAP (acme_map_v1.xlsx) and the raw pilot artifacts in the linked Drive folder.

What we ran: pilot comparisons (Nov 12–13) across A100 / H100 / L40S and representative MIG slices on your sample prompt set. Key metrics captured: TTFT (streaming & non-streaming), p50/p95/p99, sustained tokens/sec, concurrency curves, and cost per 1M tokens estimate.

High-level conclusion:
- For Acme’s latency-sensitive checkout flows (short, streaming responses), H100s give the best latency & throughput economics.
- A100 (with MIG) is cost-effective for high-density, non-latency-critical workloads.
- L40S is a reasonable middle ground for mixed traffic, but expect slightly worse TTFT on large models due to memory behavior.

Proposed MAP timeline (actionable items):
- Nov 16–18: pilot verification (we’ve completed the first pilot; we propose targeted re-runs with your dev prompts if you want deeper parity).
- Nov 22–26: full benchmarking sweep (we’ll need access to the approved sanitized prompt set and a short SSH window for live-replay).
- Dec 6: recommended fleet and cost estimate delivered (H100 + A100-MIG mix recommended).
- Dec 15: pilot go-live for selected endpoints (if approved).

Attached / Links:
- acme_map_v1.xlsx (consolidated MAP and final recommendations)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAcmeMap (perf CSVs & runbooks)
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-acme-map (contract addendum & committed capacity sketch)
- Artifacts: benchmark-results-h100.csv, a100-h100-l40s-summary.pdf

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm the sanitized prompt set for the full sweep (share link or S3 location).
2) Confirm budget / preferred commitment window so we can prepare a Dedicated quote (I’ll route to our pricing team).
3) If agreeable, please acknowledge the MAP and we’ll kick the full sweep on Nov 22.
